 This appeal coming on for orders this day, the court 
 following:
 Order

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 23.04.2022 passed by II Additional Member MACT, Indore in Claim Case No.1200263/2016 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
in the case of permanent disability of the claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,89,600/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

Shankar Nayak vs Riyaz Mansoori on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60028119/
1 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed grave error in holding the permanent disability as 40%, but the doctor calculated the permanent disability as 90%.
The Tribunal has also erred in holding compensation for attendant only for two months, while attendant is required for whole life.
so amount of compensation is just on lower side.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant as Rs.5,000/- which is on lower side.

At the time of accident, according to the circular issued by the Labour Commissioner, Govt. of MP, the minimum wages of a unskilled labour was Rs.6,850/- per month., so compensation must be assessed on the basis of income of Rs.6,850/-,
hence prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
First argument contended by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant is that Tribunal committed error in holding income of the claimant as Rs.5,000/-.
He submitted that according to the circular issued by the Labour Commissioner, Govt. of MP, the minimum wages of a unskilled labour was Rs.6,850/- per month.
So in the considered opinion of this Court just and proper amount of income in the present case would be Rs.6,850/- per month.
So the finding of the Tribunal is modified in this regard.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that Tribunal has committed error in holding just 40% of permanent disability of the claimant.
He further submits that the doctor was examined by the claimant and he stated in the examination in chief that both the hands of the claimant are of no use.
He was unable to do work she was unable to take food with his hands.
He was unable to wash by himself and also unable to take water.
The doctor further stated that both his hands are deformed and movements of both the wrists are limited to great extent.
Metarco pharyngeal joints of fingers are fixed and they are hyper extended.
Thumb movements are also restricted.
Inter pharyngeal joints are fused.
Pinching, holding actions are not possible.
The hands are of no use.
According to the doctor the bride formula percentage of disability is 90% and it is permanent.
This is part of the whole body.
8. So considering the evidence of the doctor and Ex.P-1 permanent disability certificate, it is found that claimant was unable to do anything.
So, Tribunal has committed error in holding that claimant received 40% permanent disability.
In the considered opinion of this Court, according to the evidence of the doctor, claimant is 100% disabled.
He was unable to do anything through out his life.
Hence, compensation must be assessed holding 100% permanent disability to the claimant.

9. According to the finding of the Tribunal claimant was 60 years old and adding 10% future prospects and applying multiplier of 9 the amount comes to be Rs.6850/- 10% Future Prospects x 12 x 9 = Rs.8,13,780/-.

The claimant is also entitled to get compensation under head of loss of income Shankar Nayak vs Riyaz Mansoori on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60028119/
2 during treatment, considering the injury received by the claimant, six months loss of income must be awarded i.e. 6,850/- x 6 =Rs.41,100/-.

The claimant was unable to produce any substantial evidence in regard to the medical expenses, but in the absence of medical expenses bill, Court must assess compensation in this regard with his own experience of life.
So, in this regard, in the considered opinion of this Court, claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.50,000/-.
Considering the injury, claimant is also entitled to compensation in regard to non pecuniary compensation as Rs.1,50,000/-.

10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, in the considered opinion of this Court the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side which deserves to be enhanced as under:
 Permanent Disability Rs.6,850/- 10% FP  9=Rs.8,13,780/-
 Loss of income Rs. 41,100/-
 Medical expenses Rs.50,000/-
Non pecuniary compensation Rs.1,50,000/-

Total Compensation Rs.10,54,880/-
11.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.10,54,880/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.2,89,600/- Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.7,65,280/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
12.

The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.2,00,000/- and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining enhanced amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellant within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company upto a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
13. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated herein above.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE RJ Shankar Nayak vs Riyaz Mansoori on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60028119/
